461:     /// Creates a new, empty, `DelayQueue` with the specified capacity.
462:     ///
463:     /// The queue will be able to hold at least `capacity` elements without
464:     /// reallocating. If `capacity` is 0, the queue will not allocate for
465:     /// storage.
466:     ///
467:     /// # Examples
468:     ///
469:     /// ```rust
470:     /// # use tokio_util::time::DelayQueue;
471:     /// # use std::time::Duration;
472:     ///
473:     /// # #[tokio::main]
474:     /// # async fn main() {
475:     /// let mut delay_queue = DelayQueue::with_capacity(10);
476:     ///
477:     /// // These insertions are done without further allocation
478:     /// for i in 0..10 {
479:     ///     delay_queue.insert(i, Duration::from_secs(i));
480:     /// }
481:     ///
482:     /// // This will make the queue allocate additional storage
483:     /// delay_queue.insert(11, Duration::from_secs(11));
484:     /// # }
485:     /// ```
486:     pub fn with_capacity(capacity: usize) -> DelayQueue<T> {
487:         DelayQueue {
488:             wheel: Wheel::new(),
489:             slab: SlabStorage::with_capacity(capacity),
490:             expired: Stack::default(),
491:             delay: None,
492:             wheel_now: 0,
493:             start: Instant::now(),
494:             waker: None,
495:             slot_cache: 0,
496:             occupancy_cache: 0,
497:             permit_batch: 1,
498:         }
499:     }

501:     /// Inserts `value` into the queue set to expire at a specific instant in
502:     /// time.
503:     ///
504:     /// This function is identical to `insert`, but takes an `Instant` instead
505:     /// of a `Duration`.
506:     ///
507:     /// `value` is stored in the queue until `when` is reached. At which point,
508:     /// `value` will be returned from [`poll_expired`]. If `when` has already been
509:     /// reached, then `value` is immediately made available to poll.
510:     ///
511:     /// The return value represents the insertion and is used as an argument to
512:     /// [`remove`] and [`reset`]. Note that [`Key`] is a token and is reused once
513:     /// `value` is removed from the queue either by calling [`poll_expired`] after
514:     /// `when` is reached or by calling [`remove`]. At this point, the caller
515:     /// must take care to not use the returned [`Key`] again as it may reference
516:     /// a different item in the queue.
517:     ///
518:     /// See [type] level documentation for more details.
519:     ///
520:     /// # Panics
521:     ///
522:     /// This function panics if `when` is too far in the future.
523:     ///
524:     /// # Examples
525:     ///
526:     /// Basic usage
527:     ///
528:     /// ```rust
529:     /// use tokio::time::{Duration, Instant};
530:     /// use tokio_util::time::DelayQueue;
531:     ///
532:     /// # #[tokio::main]
533:     /// # async fn main() {
534:     /// let mut delay_queue = DelayQueue::new();
535:     /// let key = delay_queue.insert_at(
536:     ///     "foo", Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(5));
537:     ///
538:     /// // Remove the entry
539:     /// let item = delay_queue.remove(&key);
540:     /// assert_eq!(*item.get_ref(), "foo");
541:     /// # }
542:     /// ```
543:     ///
544:     /// [`poll_expired`]: method@Self::poll_expired
545:     /// [`remove`]: method@Self::remove
546:     /// [`reset`]: method@Self::reset
547:     /// [`Key`]: struct@Key
548:     /// [type]: #
549:     #[track_caller]
550:     pub fn insert_at(&mut self, value: T, when: Instant) -> Key {
551:         assert!(self.slab.len() < MAX_ENTRIES, "max entries exceeded");
552: 
553:         // Normalize the deadline. Values cannot be set to expire in the past.
554:         let when = self.normalize_deadline(when);
555:         self.prepare_permit_tracking(1);
556: 
557:         // Insert the value in the store
558:         let key = self.slab.insert(Data {
559:             inner: value,
560:             when,
561:             expired: false,
562:             next: None,
563:             prev: None,
564:         });
565: 
566:         self.insert_idx(when, key);
567: 
568:         // Set a new delay if the current's deadline is later than the one of the new item
569:         let should_set_delay = if let Some(ref delay) = self.delay {
570:             let current_exp = self.normalize_deadline(delay.deadline());
571:             current_exp > when
572:         } else {
573:             true
574:         };
575: 
576:         if should_set_delay {
577:             if let Some(waker) = self.waker.take() {
578:                 waker.wake();
579:             }
580: 
581:             let delay_time = self.start + Duration::from_millis(when);
582:             if let Some(ref mut delay) = &mut self.delay {
583:                 delay.as_mut().reset(delay_time);
584:             } else {
585:                 self.delay = Some(Box::pin(sleep_until(delay_time)));
586:             }
587:         }
588: 
589:         key
590:     }

592:     /// Attempts to pull out the next value of the delay queue, registering the
593:     /// current task for wakeup if the value is not yet available, and returning
594:     /// `None` if the queue is exhausted.
595:     pub fn poll_expired(&mut self, cx: &mut task::Context<'_>) -> Poll<Option<Expired<T>>> {
596:         if !self
597:             .waker
598:             .as_ref()
599:             .map(|w| w.will_wake(cx.waker()))
600:             .unwrap_or(false)
601:         {
602:             self.waker = Some(cx.waker().clone());
603:         }
604: 
605:         let item = ready!(self.poll_idx(cx));
606:         Poll::Ready(item.map(|key| {
607:             let data = self.slab.remove(&key);
608:             debug_assert!(data.next.is_none());
609:             debug_assert!(data.prev.is_none());
610: 
611:             Expired {
612:                 key,
613:                 data: data.inner,
614:                 deadline: self.start + Duration::from_millis(data.when),
615:             }
616:         }))
617:     }
